title: deployment-stitching-and-rollback-scribe
content:
Meeting: Deployment Stitching & Rollback Scribe
Facilitator: Ethan Kim
Date: 2025-03-18
Time: 10:00-10:45 PT
Location: Zoom + #deploy-room

Attendees:
- Ethan Kim (release coordinator)
- Priya Singh (serving runtime)
- Liam O'Connor (SRE)
- Zara Mendes (platform engineering)
- Marco Liu (release automation)
- Optional: on-call engineers for Dedicated and Hosted API

Purpose / Quick TL;DR:
- Reconcile overlapping deploy windows across two release trains (train A: infra/serving-runtime changes, train B: console/rollouts UX tweaks).
- Validate rollback/runbook for the hotfix-candidate targeting NVidia driver mismatch in Dedicated pools.
- Confirm canary gating thresholds and ownership for the mid-week push.

Agenda items covered (with notes):
1) Cross-train window alignment (10:00–10:12)
- Problem: overlapping deploys tomorrow — Train A requires kernel module bump; Train B has DB migration for rollout metadata.
- Decision: Move Train B migrations to maintenance window Friday 02:00-04:00 PT; Train A goes in Thursday 22:00-23:30 PT.
- Rationale: Kernel bump is higher blast radius; we want DB migration last so rollback of Train A is simpler.
- Action: Marco to update release calendar and notify product (due 2025-03-18 15:00 PT).

2) Hotfix candidate validation & rollback rehearsal (10:12–10:28)
- Hotfix summary: Patch to pin CUDA driver shim for specific Dedicated customer pools (Jira RELEASE-412).
- Tests run: smoke on staging, perf regression check, KV-cache warmup tests passed at 10–20% load.
- Canary results: 30-minute canary in us-west-2 showed token-latency P95 increase +12% on a narrow workload slice.
- Interpretation: acceptable transient increase for this customer tier but needs closer guardrails.
- Rollback playbook reviewed:
  * Trigger conditions: error rate > 0.8% for 5m OR P95 latency > baseline +20% for 3m.
  * Rollback steps: (a) Disable route in router service, (b) revert to previous model variant in pool, (c) drain impacted nodes with rolling restart.
  * Communication: post to #deploy-room and escalation to oncall leads.
- Rehearsal notes: Liam ran a dry-run of the router disable; took ~2m. Draining a 100-node pool estimated 18–25m.
- Action: Priya to add a short-circuit to the healthcheck that will immediately mark the pool unhealthy if latency threshold exceeded (due 2025-03-19).

3) Canary gating & monitoring hooks (10:28–10:36)
- Agreed metrics to gate on: request error rate, token P95, system GPU memory pressure, KV cache miss rate.
- Observability: add a temporary alert that posts a concise summary to #canary-alerts with direct links to traces and the relevant runbook snippet.
- Action: Zara to create alert and curator dashboard (due 2025-03-19 EOD).

4) Backout sequencing for dependent services (10:36–10:42)
- Problem: console migration depends on a small schema change; if rolled back, we must ensure migration is reversible within 10 min.
- Decision: disable new console feature-flag prior to DB migration; migrations must be written reversible-first.
- Action: Train B owners to provide migration rehearse results in the next sync (owner: product-attendee, due 2025-03-19).

Open risks and notes (ranked):
- R1: Driver mismatch could escalate to many Dedicated pools if not gated — mitigation: narrow canary cohorts + quick-disable route. (Owner: Priya)
- R2: Long pool drain time may look like an outage — mitigation: pre-warm standby nodes and inform SRE-runbook to mark maintenance window. (Owner: Liam)
- R3: Human ops flash — too many concurrent owners — mitigation: single point-of-contact for 2h post-deploy (Owner: Ethan)

Action item list (clear owners, dates):
- Marco: Update release calendar and send inter-team note about shift (due 2025-03-18 15:00 PT).
- Priya: Implement healthcheck short-circuit & unit tests (due 2025-03-19 12:00 PT).
- Zara: Create canary alert and curator dashboard, include trace links (due 2025-03-19 EOD).
- Marco & Liam: Run a simulated rollback drill in staging tomorrow 09:00 PT (due 2025-03-19).
- Product owner (Train B): Provide reversible DB migration plan and feature-flag behavior doc (due 2025-03-19).

Quick change log snapshot (what will be pushed):
- Train A (Thursday 22:00): kernel/driver shim pin, serving-runtime patch, small runtime PR (#1842).
- Train B (Friday 02:00): console rollout metadata migration, feature-flag for new rollout UI.
- Hotfix-candidate: applied as canary first to 2 Dedicated pools (us-west-2-a, us-east-1-b).

Communication plan:
- Pre-deploy: brief to #deploy-room 1 hour before window (Marco).
- During canary: automated summary to #canary-alerts; human SRE triage on call (Liam).
- Post-deploy: 1-hour postmortem note if rollback triggered, full retrospective if any customer impact.

Notes to follow up in write-up / next sync:
- Confirm whether we should automate route disable when alert fires (worth quick spike in infra automation).
- Decide on canary cohort membership policy (should be explicit for Dedicated tier customers).
- Track the latency delta root cause if P95 continues to drift after healthcheck change.

Misc / attic thoughts (informal):
- Consider a small synthetic query load that mimics customer KV hit patterns during canary to better surface cache regressions.
- Might be useful to pre-seed standby nodes in Dedicated pools for faster rollback (ops cost vs user-facing downtime tradeoff).

Meeting adjourned 10:45 PT — notes captured by Ethan.

File notes: draft-ish; please add inline corrections. This is meant to be an actionable operational scribe (keep as short checklist + runbook links).
